data.title: Anthropic's stock surges in its debut - and the rest of the market dives anyway
data.description:
By Joy Wiltermuth and Joseph Adinolfi

All four major U.S. stock indexes are now on pace for their worst week since President Trump's 'liberation day' tariffs of April 2025

The stock market is convulsing despite a hugely successful IPO from Anthropic on Thursday.

Neither a wildly successful first-ever IPO from an artificial-intelligence lab, nor a blockbuster earnings report from arguably the most important company in the AI trade, were enough to stop the carnage in the U.S. stock market this week.

Earlier this week, Nvidia (NVDA) passed a big "earnings test" after the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang - but its stock fell anyway. Then, on Thursday, Anthropic's (ANT) hugely anticipated IPO passed the market's next big "valuation test," with the AI lab's stock opening 34% above its $83 IPO price, before it closed at $97.17.

Yet the S&P 500 index SPX still tumbled 2% Thursday to close at 7,175.83, as a broad-based selloff left each of the index's 11 sectors in the red for a second time in three days, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

"I'm a bit surprised that we are cascading here," said Mark Arbeter, president of Arbeter Investments. He expected Nivida's earnings and Anthropic's successful IPO to calm the market, allow it to bottom "at least on a short-term basis" and open the door to "a decent snapback rally."

Instead, the S&P 500 stayed below its 200-day moving average, a crucial support level, and was edging closer to the 7,000 mark. Any close below 7,037.04 would officially land the S&P 500 in a correction, or a drop of at least 10% from its previous peak, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

To be sure, corrections of 10% are considered normal, and the stock market isn't the U.S. economy, which lately has been showing signs of speeding up.

"Technically, it's been a long time since we've had a significant downturn in the market, and I think we are due," said David Kelly, chief global strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management. "I don't think it's much more than that."

Kelly doesn't think "the amount of money raised by Anthropic sucked the market dry." Instead, if there's any problem, it's that people's portfolios have become overly concentrated, he said. Furthermore, he thinks nothing about the economy's resilience has changed. "People should try to stay calm," he added.

Still, while past dips in stocks were bought, now there appears to be "a lot of loose hands holding equities right now," said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist at LPL Financial.

Lately, when stocks have opened higher, the market has failed to hold those gains through the close. Turnquist noted. "Sentiment has clearly changed in the market," he said.

To put a finer point on the scope of Thursday's selloff, only 38 stocks in the S&P 500 rose on Thursday - the fewest since Dec. 31, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The heavy losses had the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA down 6.2% for the week and teetering on the edge of correction territory.

The S&P 500 was off 5.1% for the week, while the Nasdaq Composite COMP was 5% lower and the Russell 2000 index RUT of small-cap stocks was off 4.9%. If those declines hold, it would be the worst week for all four indexes since the "liberation day" tariff selloff in the week of April 4, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

-Joy Wiltermuth -Joseph Adinolfi

data.title: Overseas Revenue Up 171.5% YoY, Contributing Nearly Half of Total Revenue; Record High Quarterly Robotaxi Revenue of Over RMB100 Million; Third Quarter 2026 Revenue of RMB321.5 Million, Up 88.0% YoY; Gross Margin Reached 43.0%

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- WeRide Inc. (“WeRide” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: WRD; HKEX: 0800), a global leader in autonomous driving technology, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Operational and Financial Highlights

  • Revenue grew 88.0% and gross margin expanded to 43.0%, driven primarily by the overseas business. Total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB321.5 million (US$48.0 million), representing an increase of 88.0% year over year and 38.8% quarter over quarter. Gross margin reached 43.0%, up 10.1 percentage points year over year. Revenue from higher-margin overseas operations was RMB146.9 million (US$21.9 million), up 171.5% year over year, and accounted for 45.7% of total revenue.
  • AI Infrastructure revenue nearly doubled, capturing fast-growing data demand from Physical AI. Leveraging the closed‑loop data capabilities built over years of autonomous‑driving operations, Jingshuo Technology, WeRide’s Physical AI Infrastructure (“AI Infrastructure”) subsidiary, serves customers across embodied AI, robotics, autonomous driving and foundation models, with end‑to‑end solutions spanning pre‑training data, post‑training environments and trusted verification. Driven by surging demand for high-quality physical-world data, revenue from this business nearly doubled year over year.
  • Quarterly Robotaxi revenue surpassed RMB100 million; Guangzhou operations achieved positive unit economics. In the third quarter of 2026, Robotaxi revenue exceeded RMB100 million for the first time, up 204.0% year over year, with overseas markets contributing more than 90% of total Robotaxi revenue. The Company’s Robotaxi operations in Guangzhou achieved positive unit economics, marking an important milestone in validating the economics of Robotaxi operations at scale.
  • Global L4 fleet of approximately 4,100 vehicles; Robotaxi fleet up 26% quarter over quarter. As of October 31, 2026, the Company’s global L4 fleet comprised approximately 4,100 vehicles, including more than 2,300 Robotaxis. The Robotaxi fleet increased by 26% quarter over quarter.
  • WeRide secured Spain’s first national operating permit for L4 autonomous passenger vehicles, accelerating commercialization in Europe. The Company received Spain’s first L4 autonomous passenger vehicle operating permit from the Spanish Directorate-General for Traffic (“DGT”), laying the groundwork for commercial services in Spain. The Company also advanced its operations in Switzerland, Belgium and France, and began road testing in Slovakia, while continuing to expand its collaboration with local public transportation operators.
  • Asset-light expansion accelerating in the Middle East, with a fleet of approximately 600 vehicles. The Company continues to expand its operating fleet and service areas in the Middle East, targeting full coverage of the core urban areas of Abu Dhabi and Dubai by year-end. The Company’s Middle East fleet reached approximately 600 vehicles, up approximately 50% from about 400 vehicles as of July 31, 2026. As of the date of this release, WeRide is Uber’s largest autonomous vehicle partner outside the United States, measured by the number of fully driverless Robotaxis operating on its platform.
  • L2++/L3 mass production accelerating, with cumulative WRD 3.0 deliveries exceeding 100,000 units. Now, the AION i60, GAC Trumpchi Yue 7 and AION Ray7, all equipped with the Company’s WRD 3.0 one-stage end-to-end L2++/L3 solution, were launched, extending the solution’s adoption across more production models and driving scenarios. By the end of the quarter, cumulative deliveries of WRD 3.0 exceeded 100,000 units. The Company continued to expand its partnership network, establishing collaborations with several leading OEM groups.

L4 Business Update

Robotaxi Business Update

In the third quarter of 2026, Robotaxi revenue exceeded RMB100 million for the first time, representing an increase of 204.0% year over year, with overseas markets contributing more than 90% of total Robotaxi revenue.

International Operations

  • Overseas Robotaxi revenue grew rapidly, supported by the Company’s high-margin, asset-light business model. In overseas markets, the Company provides autonomous driving technology and remote assistance, while local partners provide fleet investment and handle other operations. This division of roles enables the Company to continue scaling deployments across Europe and the Middle East with greater capital efficiency.
  • The Middle East fleet expanded, with broader coverage of core urban areas. The Company continued to expand its Middle East fleet to approximately 600 Robotaxis and extend its operating areas in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, now covering the major districts of both cities’ core urban areas. This lays the foundation for broader service coverage and future operational growth.
  • WeRide obtained Spain’s first national L4 autonomous driving permit and advanced its Madrid deployment. In September 2026, the Company, together with Uber and AVOMO, received Spain's first L4 autonomous passenger vehicle operating permit from the DGT, allowing vehicles to be deployed on public roads. The permit authorizes testing of WeRide’s GXR autonomous vehicles in Spain and marks the beginning of mapping in the Madrid region ahead of the Company’s first joint launch in Europe.
  • L4 deployments and services in Switzerland and Slovakia continued to advance. Along with its partners, Schweizerische Bundesbahnen (“SBB”) and Swiss Transit Lab (“STL”), the Company launched public Robotaxi services in Canton of Zurich. In Slovakia, the first batch of Robotaxis began road testing, building operating experience to support future deployments.
  • Robotaxi services in Asia continued to expand. In Singapore, the Company continued to expand its Robotaxi service together with Grab and had provided more than 20,000 L4 autonomous driving rides as of the end of the third quarter of 2026.

China Operations

  • Guangzhou operations achieved positive unit economics, with further improvements in operational efficiency. In the third quarter of 2026, domestic Robotaxi operations achieved an average of 21 daily orders per vehicle, with a peak of 33 orders per vehicle in one day. Cumulative registered users continued to grow rapidly, up 143.5% from the end of the previous quarter.
  • Service areas in key cities continued to expand. In Guangzhou, the Company’s Robotaxi service covers Tianhe, Haizhu and the core districts of Huangpu. These developments provide a solid foundation for further scaling the Company’s Robotaxi business.

Other L4 Business Updates

  • Robobus achieved one of Europe’s first fully driverless services. At Zurich Airport, the Company’s Robobus now operates without an onboard safety operator, making it one of the first fully driverless Robobus services in Europe. The Company is also advancing autonomous driving collaborations with public transportation operators such as Keolis in France and expanding its Robobus operations in Belgium. In Slovakia, the Robobus fleet has arrived and commenced testing.
  • Robosweeper expanded its presence in Singapore. The Company has partnered with leading environmental services providers, Chye Thiam Maintenance and RE Sustainability, to deliver sanitation services across key locations including Marina Coastal Drive, the Esplanade and Sentosa Island, with further deployments expected in the near term.

L2++/L3 Business Update

  • Cumulative deliveries exceeded 100,000 units, with a growing mass-production pipeline. As of the end of the quarter, cumulative deliveries of the Company’s WRD 3.0 L2++/L3 solution exceeded 100,000 units. During the quarter, the Company secured 10 new L2++/L3 mass-production design wins, further expanding its pipeline of future production programs.
  • Customer base and design-win portfolio continued to expand. The Company secured multiple new design wins from several leading OEMs, further validating the competitiveness of its technology and expanding its customer reach.
  • The Company’s L2++/L3 solution continued to demonstrate its capabilities in driving competitions. Customer vehicles equipped with the Company’s L2++/L3 solution have won eight championships in the China Intelligent Driving Competition, further demonstrating the solution’s overall technical capabilities.

AI Infrastructure Business Update

High-quality real-world data and verifiable training environments are key enablers for the development of Physical AI foundation models.

  • End-to-end capabilities covering the full path from pre-training to continuous learning. Building on the closed-loop data capabilities developed through the Company’s autonomous driving operations, Jingshuo provides pre-training data, post-training environments and trusted verification across the full path from pre-training to continuous learning. Its capabilities span data collection, quality control and annotation, synthetic data generation, environment construction, independent evaluation and post-training integration. It offers high-quality datasets, licensing of data-processing software and post-training environments, and customized data services to customers in autonomous driving, foundation models, embodied AI and robotics.
  • A three-layer product suite and two engines, closing the “collection–assetization–training” loop.  Jingshuo’s product stack comprises three layers. EGOK is a proprietary wearable multimodal collection terminal with hardware-level synchronization. SkillForge turns first-person operation data into trainable, verifiable and licensable skill assets with task definitions and success criteria. Crucible is an environment hub that connects tasks into executable, independently judged environments and supports post-training integration. Two engines connect the layers: the Data Engine turns experience into versioned data and skills, and the World Engine, powered by the GENESIS-Robotics world model, turns real-world demonstrations into verifiable training environments.
  • High-quality multimodal data assets support applications across diverse real-world scenarios. Through automated 3D reconstruction, multimodal alignment and fine-grained annotation, Jingshuo has built a large-scale dataset library serving foundation model, embodied AI and robotics customers in China and overseas.

Management Commentary

Tony Han, WeRide’s Founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer, stated, “This quarter showed that our global strategy is working. Overseas markets now generate nearly half of our total revenue and more than 90% of our Robotaxi revenue. Operating driverless fleets in foreign markets is challenging, which is exactly why it is becoming our long-term moat. With new deployments in Europe and a Middle East fleet of approximately 600 vehicles, WeRide is now Uber’s largest autonomous vehicle partner outside the United States by driverless fleet size. In China, our Guangzhou Robotaxi operations achieved positive unit economics, demonstrating that Robotaxi can be a sustainable business. Robotaxi is our core business and the fastest path to commercializing Physical AI. The technology and closed-loop data we have built on real roads now power three mutually reinforcing businesses: Robotaxi, L2++/L3 solutions, and AI Infrastructure, which extends these capabilities to foundation models, embodied AI and robotics. As an infrastructure builder for Physical AI, we are just getting started.”

Jennifer Li, WeRide’s Chief Financial Officer and Head of International, added, “This quarter, revenue grew by 88% to RMB321.5 million, gross margin reached 43%, and overseas revenue made up nearly half of the total. Our asset-light model enables us to expand quickly and efficiently. Based on our operating plan, we have more than four years of cash runway, sufficient to fully fund our path to self-sustaining cash flow. More importantly, we are building a long-term moat. Operating across 13 countries and holding permits in 9 requires years of regulatory trust and operational experience — this is hard to replicate. We will translate this lead into sustainable, profitable growth.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Revenue

Total revenue grew 88.0% year over year to RMB321.5 million (US$48.0 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB171.0 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the expansion of the Company’s Robotaxi-centered L4 business, rapid growth in the L2++/L3 business and continued growth in the AI Infrastructure business.

Cost of Revenue

Cost of revenue was RMB183.4 million (US$27.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB114.7 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in cost of revenue was in line with revenue growth in the Robotaxi-centered L4 business and the AI Infrastructure business.

Gross Profit and Gross Margin

Gross profit was RMB138.1 million (US$20.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB56.3 million in the same period of 2025. Gross margin was 43.0% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 32.9% in the same period of 2025. Gross margin expansion was mainly driven by revenue growth in the high-margin overseas business and the L2++/L3 business.

Operating Expenses

Operating expenses were RMB505.7 million (US$75.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB435.8 million in the same period of 2025.

  • R&D expenses were RMB465.3 million (US$69.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB316.4 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in R&D expenses was primarily due to the increase in personnel and outsourcing labor costs, outsourced R&D expenses and cloud service fees. In addition, from July 1, 2026, the estimated useful lives of IDC-related equipment were uniformly extended to six years, resulting in lower depreciation and amortization expenses.
     
  • Administrative expenses were RMB13.9 million (US$2.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB100.4 million in the same period of 2025. The significant decrease in administrative expenses was primarily due to a reversal of share-based compensation expenses resulting from employee departures, and a decrease in professional service fees, as the same period of 2025 included fees related to the global offering.
     
  • Selling expenses were RMB26.5 million (US$4.0 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB19.0 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in selling expenses was primarily due to the increase in sales personnel costs.

Loss for the Period

  • Loss for the period was RMB310.0 million (US$46.2 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB307.3 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Non-IFRS adjusted loss1 for the period was RMB336.5 million (US$50.2 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB275.6 million in the same period of 2025.

Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (“EBITDA”)2

EBITDA was negative RMB246.4 million (US$36.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, an improvement of 2.9% from negative RMB253.7 million in the same period of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Loss per Ordinary Share and per ADS3  

  • Basic and diluted loss per ordinary share was RMB0.32 (US$0.05) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.34 in the same period of 2025.
     
  • Basic and diluted loss per ADS was RMB0.96 (US$0.15) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB1.02 in the same period of 2025.

____________________________
1 Non-IFRS adjusted loss for the period is defined as loss for the period excluding share-based compensation expenses and fair value changes of financial assets at FVTPL.
2 EBITDA is defined as loss for the period excluding income tax, finance costs and depreciation and amortization expenses.
3 Each ADS represents three Class A ordinary shares.

Balance Sheet

As of September 30, 2026, WeRide held RMB3,846.5 million (US$573.7 million) in cash and cash equivalents and time deposits, RMB797.7 million (US$119.0 million) in investments in wealth management products, which were recorded in current financial assets at FVTPL, and RMB18.8 million (US$2.8 million) in restricted cash, for an aggregate amount of RMB4,663.0 million (US$695.5 million).

Exchange Rate Information

Unless otherwise noted, all translations from RMB to US$ were made at a rate of RMB6.7045 to US$1.00, the exchange rate in effect as of September 30, 2026, as set forth in the H.10 statistical release of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. The Company makes no representation that any RMB or US$ amounts could have been, or could be, converted into US$ or RMB, as the case may be, at any particular rate, or at all.

Use of Non-IFRS Financial Measures

In evaluating its business, the Company considers and uses the non-IFRS financial measures of (i) adjusted loss for the period and (ii) EBITDA as supplemental measures to review and assess operating performance. The Company believes that adjusted loss for the period and EBITDA provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating the Company’s consolidated results of operations in the same manner as it helps the Company’s management. The Company defines adjusted loss for the period as loss for the period excluding share-based compensation expenses and fair value changes of financial assets at FVTPL. The Company defines EBITDA as loss for the period excluding income tax, finance costs, depreciation and amortization expenses.

The Company presents the non-IFRS financial measures because they are used by its management to evaluate its operating performance and formulate business plans. Adjusted loss for the period enables the Company’s management to assess the Company’s operating results without considering the impact of the aforementioned non-cash adjustment items that it does not consider to be indicative of its core operations. EBITDA enables the Company’s management to assess the Company’s operating results without considering the impact of income tax, finance costs, and depreciation and amortization, and to focus more on operating cash items. Accordingly, the Company believes that the use of these non-IFRS financial measures provides useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating its operating results in the same manner as its management and board of directors.

These non-IFRS financial measures are not defined under IFRS and are not presented in accordance with IFRS. The non-IFRS financial measures have limitations as analytical tools. One of the key limitations of using the non-IFRS financial measures is that they do not reflect all items of expenses that affect the Company’s operations. The non-IFRS financial measures should not be considered in isolation or construed as alternatives to loss for the period or any other measure of performance information prepared and presented in accordance with IFRS or as an indicator of the Company’s operating performance. data.title: MasTec Enters into Definitive Agreement to Acquire Murphy Corporation, a Leading Mechanical Contractor Serving Mission-Critical End Markets
data.description:
MasTec Enters into Definitive Agreement to Acquire Murphy Corporation, a Leading Mechanical Contractor Serving Mission-Critical End Markets

  • Adds One of the Nation's Leading Mechanical Platforms with More Than 119 Years of Operating History and Approximately 1,600 Employees, Including 1,200 Union Craft Workforce
  • Enhances Technical Capabilities Through Industry-Leading Engineering, Prefabrication, Preconstruction and Self-Perform Execution Expertise
  • Expands MasTec's Participation in Fast-Growing Mission-Critical Infrastructure Markets Including Aviation and Defense, Pharmaceutical, Healthcare, Technology and Advanced Manufacturing
  • Creates Significant Opportunities to Expand Recurring Service and Maintenance Revenue Supporting Operational Data Centers and Other Diversified Markets
  • Expected to Be Immediately Accretive to Revenue, Earnings Per Share, Adjusted EBITDA and Cash Flow from Operations

MasTec, Inc. (NYSE: MTZ) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Murphy Corporation ("Murphy"), one of the largest and most respected mechanical contractors (“the Transaction”) in the United States. Founded in 1907 and continuously family owned and operated for more than 119 years, Murphy has built a scaled, full-service platform providing mechanical, plumbing and process infrastructure solutions across mission-critical end markets. With approximately 1,200 highly skilled union craft professionals and national execution capabilities, Murphy serves a diversified portfolio of customers in aviation and defense, healthcare, pharmaceutical manufacturing, technology, food processing, refrigeration and advanced manufacturing, supported by industry-leading engineering, preconstruction and fabrication capabilities. Murphy's experienced management team, led by President and Chief Executive Officer Patrick Murphy, will remain in place following the Transaction.

In addition to its large-scale construction capabilities, Murphy maintains a substantial service and maintenance business providing recurring HVAC, plumbing, refrigeration, controls and other mechanical services to mission-critical facilities as well as other market sectors. MasTec believes this business is positioned for significant growth as Murphy expands its owner-direct relationships and supports the increasing number of data centers and other large-load facilities transitioning from construction into ongoing operation. This recurring service revenue complements Murphy’s project-based operations, strengthens customer relationships and enhances the resilience and visibility of its financial performance. For the two years ended March 31, 2026, Murphy delivered strong double-digit growth in both revenue and EBITDA, driven by increasing demand for mission-critical infrastructure, strong customer relationships and consistent execution for its customers. Murphy is projected to generate full calendar year 2026 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $775 million and approximately $140 million, respectively. Murphy will serve as a new operating group of MasTec, and Murphy’s financial results are expected to be reflected in the Clean Energy and Infrastructure Segment.

Jose Mas, MasTec’s Chief Executive Officer, commented, "We are excited to welcome Murphy and its talented team members to the MasTec family. Murphy has built one of the premier integrated mechanical contracting businesses in the United States through exceptional customer service, operational excellence and an unwavering commitment to safety. Just as importantly, Murphy has built a culture that closely aligns with MasTec's values, including a commitment to entrepreneurship, accountability, safety, long-term relationships and taking care of its people.

“Murphy expands MasTec’s capabilities in some of the fastest growing and most diverse infrastructure markets in North America. Its highly skilled union craft workforce, supported by established apprenticeship, training and field-leadership programs, provides the labor capacity and execution expertise required to deliver large, complex projects safely and efficiently. Together, we will be able to provide customers with a broader range of self-perform infrastructure services across both the construction and operational phases of mission-critical facilities.

“We believe Murphy's differentiated market position, strong recurring service and maintenance revenue, attractive margin profile and substantial growth opportunities make it an exceptional strategic fit for MasTec and a highly compelling investment for our shareholders."

Patrick Murphy, President and CEO of Murphy, commented, “For over 100 years, our family has had the privilege of leading a company built by outstanding employees and trusted by exceptional customers. As we considered the future of Murphy, it was important to find a partner that shared our commitment to safety, integrity, operational excellence and enduring relationships.

“We found that partner in the MasTec family. Their reputation for execution, entrepreneurial culture and commitment to investing in people made this a natural fit. By joining MasTec, we will be able to provide additional opportunities for our employees, expand the capabilities we bring to our customers and continue building on the legacy that has defined Murphy for more than a century.

“Most importantly, our customers, employees and partners can expect continuity from the team and culture that have made Murphy successful, while benefiting from the scale and resources of one of North America's leading infrastructure companies.”

Transaction Rationale

Expands MasTec's Participation Across Mission-Critical Infrastructure: Murphy adds leading mechanical, plumbing, HVAC and process infrastructure capabilities serving highly attractive and diverse end markets. Together, MasTec and Murphy will provide a broader range of self-perform infrastructure solutions “inside the fence”.

Adds A Scarce, Scaled Mechanical Infrastructure Platform: Murphy is among the largest mechanical contractors in the United States, with over 100 years of operating history, approximately 1,600 employees, including approximately 1,200 highly skilled union craft professionals, national execution capabilities and one of the most experienced leadership teams in the industry. Opportunities to acquire assets of this scale and quality are infrequent.

Enhances Technical Capabilities and Execution Certainty: Murphy brings differentiated engineering, preconstruction, virtual design, prefabrication capabilities and building information modeling that support project execution, labor productivity, schedule certainty and quality performance. These capabilities create meaningful value for customers and represent significant barriers to entry within the industry.

Highly Complementary Culture and Leadership Team: Murphy's family ownership, people-first culture, commitment to safety and operational excellence closely align with MasTec's values and operating philosophy. The Transaction preserves an experienced leadership team while providing additional resources to support continued growth and long-term customer success.

Deepens Relationships with Leading Infrastructure Customers: Murphy serves a diversified base of blue-chip customers and project partners across critical infrastructure markets, supported by longstanding relationships and a proven track record delivering large, complex projects safely and successfully. The combination creates opportunities to expand services with existing customers and pursue larger opportunities together.

Immediate Financial Contributions with Significant Long-Term Growth Opportunities: Murphy has demonstrated a consistent track record of growth, profitability and cash flow generation supported by strong backlog visibility, recurring service and maintenance revenue and favorable long-term trends across its end markets. MasTec expects meaningful opportunities to expand Murphy’s service business by supporting the growing installed base of operational data centers and other diverse facilities, including facilities where Murphy’s construction relationships and knowledge provide a natural foundation for ongoing maintenance and support. MasTec expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, earnings per share and cash flow from operations.

Transaction Overview

The purchase price is approximately $1.25 billion payable in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments. Additionally, there is a potential earnout payment based on the cumulative three-year financial performance of Murphy post-closing. MasTec has arranged to finance the Transaction with a bank term loan entered into contemporaneously with the Transaction agreement. MasTec’s September 30, 2026 pro forma net leverage is estimated to be 2.7x with further deleveraging expected to reduce net leverage to less than 2.0x during calendar year 2027. Substantially all conditions to closing have been satisfied and MasTec expects to close the transaction expeditiously.

McDermott Will & Schulte LLP and Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP are serving as MasTec's Transaction and financing legal advisors, respectively. Sable Capital, LLC is serving as financial advisor to Murphy, and Holland & Knight LLP as its legal advisor.

About MasTec

MasTec, Inc. is a leading North American infrastructure engineering and construction company focused primarily on engineering, building, installation, maintenance and upgrade of communications, energy and utility and other infrastructure. MasTec primarily operates under four business segments including Communications, serving both wireless and wireline/fiber infrastructure; Power Delivery, serving primarily utility customers in transmission, distribution and large load electrical infrastructure markets; Pipeline Infrastructure serving energy and other customers with installation and maintenance services primarily for natural gas pipeline and distribution infrastructure; and Clean Energy and Infrastructure, providing renewable energy engineering and construction services, as well as for heavy civil and other industrial infrastructure markets. Learn more at www.mastec.com.

About Murphy

Murphy is a premier national contractor designing, constructing, and maintaining mechanical systems for the commercial, industrial, and institutional markets with unique capabilities to manage complex and demanding projects. We continually innovate and improve our business processes to maximize value for our customers and to better our company’s performance. We achieve this through safety excellence, empowerment of our people, effective teamwork, development of our partners, and dedicated customer focus. To learn more, visit www.murphynet.com.

data.title: barq Signs MoU with TenPay Global to Enhance Remittances and Digital Payments in China
data.description:
SINGAPORE, SG / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / barq, a leading Saudi fintech company, has signed a strategic memorandum of understanding (MoU) with TenPay Global, Tencent's cross-border payment platform, to develop international remittance solutions and expand digital payment services in China. The signing took place on the sidelines of barq's participation in the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026, one of the world's leading gatherings for fintech and innovation.

The MoU was signed by Ahmed Alenazi, Founder and CEO of barq, and Wenhui Yang, CEO of TenPay Global (Singapore). The agreement reflects barq's commitment to expanding its international partnerships and strengthening integration with global payment ecosystems.

Under the MoU, the two companies will work to enable barq users to transfer funds directly to recipients' wallets through the Weixin app in mainland China. They will also work to enable QR code payments at tens of millions of merchants that accept Weixin Pay, offering users a more convenient and flexible financial experience.

The partnership will allow barq to benefit from TenPay Global's network of more than 60 international banks and remittance institutions, which supports remittances to China from over 150 countries and regions, with funds potentially arriving within one minute, 24 hours a day, seven days a week. It also paves the way for barq to join an ecosystem of more than 60 international digital wallets from 16 countries and regions, enabling their users to make payments at merchants in China through Weixin Pay.

Commenting on the signing, Ahmed Alenazi, Founder and CEO of barq, said: "This partnership marks a strategic step in our international expansion and reflects our commitment to building meaningful partnerships with leading global financial and technology companies to develop digital financial solutions that transcend geographical boundaries. Through our collaboration with TenPay Global, we look forward to strengthening financial connectivity between Saudi Arabia and China and providing our users with a faster, more convenient experience in remittances and digital payments."

Wenhui Yang, CEO of TenPay Global (Singapore), emphasized that cross-border payments are more effective when integrated into the services people use every day. He highlighted the importance of collaborating with strong local partners to connect digital wallets with the Weixin ecosystem without requiring users to change their familiar payment habits. He added that TenPay Global sees promising growth opportunities in the Middle East and that this partnership represents an important step toward strengthening financial connectivity between the region and China.

The agreement builds on barq's growth since its establishment in 2023. Its user base has surpassed 15 million users, representing more than 210 nationalities, and it achieved unicorn status in September 2026 after completing a USD 329.5 million Series A funding round. These milestones reflect barq's growing standing in the fintech sector and its ambition to expand its global presence, in line with Saudi Vision 2030 and the Financial Sector Development Program.

data.title: 'Nvidia's turmoil has me spooked': Should I sell my stocks and buy real estate - or ride out the storm?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Tempted to ditch stocks for property or CDs? Take a deep breath before making any sudden moves.

Quentin Fottrell: "I'm not convinced a spooked investor is the one most likely to make a smart move."

Investors are nervous. Again.

A Moneyist reader nearing retirement shared his fears: "With the market dropping so sharply, is this a good time to move some money out of investments in the S&P 500 SPX and consider other opportunities? I'm in my late 60s. Nvidia's turmoil has me spooked, so I'm looking at a couple of options."

"Real estate here in Florida seems to be presenting some interesting opportunities, with plenty of inventory and sellers who appear more willing to negotiate," he wrote. "Another possibility is moving some money into CDs, which are currently offering much more attractive interest rates."

It's a common knee-jerk reaction, and he may be overreacting. A drop isn't a crash, even when it feels like one. The market fell sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic, and again after President Trump announced a trade war with multiple countries, including China. Both times, it recovered. And, yes, it's falling again this week amid Nvidia's woes.

The stock market regularly shows its teeth. It's the nature of the beast.

I'm not convinced a spooked investor is the one most likely to make a smart move. It never ceases to amaze me how quickly people panic when the market turns south. But the market regularly shows its teeth. It's the nature of the beast. After Nvidia's earnings were released on Tuesday afternoon, you better believe that analysts have questions.

The latest roar came from Nvidia (NVDA). CEO Jensen Huang resigned last week after admitting he had been unfaithful to his wife amid reports of an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence agencies reportedly suspect of ties to Chinese intelligence. He also reportedly had relationships with two other Nvidia employees.

Bernstein senior semiconductor analyst Stacy Rasgon cut his rating on Nvidia's stock to "market perform" from "outperform," and halved his price target to $200 a share. Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer cut the stock to "perform" from "outperform" and removed his price target. (Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment.)

Take the long view. Year to date as of Thursday afternoon, the S&P 500 has risen 4.6%, the Nasdaq Composite COMP has increased 2.7%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA is up 1.5%, and the Russell 2000 RUT has gained 6.9%. Keep in mind, the market has been bumpy, with recent volatility driven by shaken confidence in AI-related stocks.

Related: Nvidia's leadership saga unfolds as demand is surging for Anthropic's IPO

Weathering storms

Nvidia is one of the largest components of major stock market indexes, with a market capitalization of $3.75 trillion as of Wednesday afternoon. Its performance is closely watched alongside that of other AI-related stocks, including Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Intel (INTC), Micron Technology (MU), Dell Technologies (DELL) and Oracle (ORCL).

You could regard this as the long-awaited AI bubble bursting (although the AI revolution is likely here to stay). You might see it as an overdue correction. Or you could view these events as another "monster of the week," a TV trope that mirrors real-life market panics.

If that volatility has you looking for safer ground, CD rates are reaching up to 5% if you are prepared to lock up your money for anywhere from six months to five years. CDs are better suited for short-term, safe-haven savings like an emergency fund rather than making up a significant part of your long-term investment plan.

You could choose to view these latest events as another 'monster of the week.'

The stock market has weathered quite a few storms in recent years. The more you check your stocks, however, the more apt you are to fret over the volatility, and the more likely you are to sell based on growing fear, unease, and uncertainty.

The geopolitical backdrop - the unpredictable and frankly confusing war in Iran, Russia's invasion of Ukraine and Trump's on-again, off-again trade war - has made many investors and 401(k) account holders nervous and led to fears of a broader correction.

As you move from your 40s into your 50s and 60s, the share of your portfolio invested in stocks typically shifts to reflect the time you have to recover from a major market correction and to mitigate what's known as sequence-of-returns risk.

That risk is especially critical in the years just before and after retirement. A large market decline early in retirement can severely damage your portfolio far more than a similar decline happening many years later. Ultimately, the right asset allocation will depend on your personal risk tolerance.

Don't miss: 'God works in mysterious ways': I became a Nvidia millionaire playing 'World of Warcraft.' Am I smart - or just lucky?

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Buying real estate

Selling shares that you presumably hope will see you through retirement to invest in real estate is a dramatic move. The Florida property market is as good as any to use as an example: The average home value in Florida is approximately $375,000, down 0.5% over the past year, with homes going to "pending" in around 47 days on average, according to Zillow (Z).

As the Moneyist reader points out, the Florida real estate market has fallen and stabilized, with single-family and luxury homes showing resilience. Condos, meanwhile, have had a rougher time due to oversupply and softening demand, compounded by persistently high interest rates and regulatory costs.

Stocks and real estate can both provide passive income, but are you ready to be an absentee landlord and shoulder the costs that come with it because of a bad week or month in the stock market? Good luck with those property taxes and storm insurance premiums.

Take a long, sober look at your portfolio. It will take your mind off Nvidia.

Deals exist in the Sunshine State and elsewhere. Florida's new-build construction market has remained resilient in the face of rising inventory, despite higher rates. Major homebuilders are offering aggressive incentives to buyers who use their in-house lenders. That particular trend is happening nationwide, too.

In November, 46% of homebuilders cut prices, the highest share since COVID-19, according to a monthly survey by the National Association of Home Builders released Tuesday. The average price cut remained steady at 6% for an eighth consecutive month. Meanwhile, 68% of builders offered sales incentives - also a post-COVID high.

For better or for worse - and with AI's help recently - the stock market is a beast that keeps on roaring. Over the last 10 years, the S&P 500 gained more than 230% in value compared to roughly 84% for U.S. residential home prices, analysts say, and that's before factoring in dividends or the costs of owning a home.

If you're considering a big portfolio change today or tomorrow, you need an adviser who can take a long, sober look at your allocations, age, retirement plans and goals, your investing timeline, your mix of U.S. versus overseas stocks, and your holdings in bonds and cash. All that work will take your mind off Nvidia.

data.title: Citi warns a key stock-market signal is close to flashing red
data.description:
By Jules Rimmer

Citi strategists worry about Nvidia financing, sectoral rotation and copper weakness

Citi says its 'generals' framework is about to flash red on Monday.

A stock-market signal employed by strategists at Citigroup is close to flashing red.

"To control for the fact that we may not be prescient enough to call the top, we have introduced the 'Generals' concept, which essentially suggests that it is a good risk management tool to take off equity risk whenever the bubble leadership breaks down," say global market strategists led by Dirk Willer, in a note to clients.

They define this as when four of the top seven stocks by market capitalization in the S&P 500 break below their 200-day moving average and stay for at least five days. By Monday, it's likely that this signal triggers, the strategists say.

Those four stocks are: Meta Platforms (META), Broadcom (AVGO), Alphabet (GOOGL) and Nvidia (NVDA).

"The generals work by removing downside tails, not necessarily by having a very high standalone hit ratio. But there are enough warning signs to our mind, to heed the signal here," the strategists say.

Front and center of Citi's concerns is the stock most in focus for the last fortnight: Nvidia (NVDA) . Willer and team note that 10% of Nvidia's revenues came from China and Hong Kong, and with export licenses there under review in wake of the Jensen Huang scandal, that is a risk.

The team also worries about the extent of Nvidia's financing exposure to the whole AI ecosystem. The company has a guarantee exposure of $118 billion, $10 billion up from the previous quarter, it has $32 billion of financial backstops to neocloud operators, $20 billion of future equity commitments and $74 billion of data-center leases. All of which makes some analysts decidedly queasy.

The Citi report identifies uncomfortable parallels between the current rotation among sectors and other periods of market duress in 2000 and late 2021. These bouts of volatility were characterized by an "aggressive change in leadership" where growth and momentum stocks lost favor compared to quality and value. In both instances, the S&P 500 SPX and Nasdaq NDX suffered major drawdowns. An aggressive shift from cyclicals into defensives also raises a yellow flag.

Huge factor rotation is a warning sign for SPX

"Overall," the report observes, "the price action under the hood is not overly reassuring."

Citi is also concerned about the message that copper-price weakness is transmitting. Copper (HG00) has long been interpreted by analysts as an indicator of overall economic growth and Citi eliminated its buy recommendation on the commodity at the end of October. The London price of copper has tumbled from a high of around $14,700 per metric ton to just $12,500 now. The relationship of copper to growth, as suggested by the Institute for Supply Management survey, suggests a downturn in the economic cycle is looming. A strong dollar is also detrimental to copper prices.

Bonds rally when copper falls

If the AI bubble does burst, the Citi team recommend investors turn to bonds, not just because of the direct contribution from the AI buildout but also a negative wealth effect.

"Now we are at 240% of GDP. A meaningful sell-off of a much larger market, may create more economic damage," say the strategists.

They concede the timing is not easy. In 2000, the Fed hiked once more after the Nasdaq 100 NDX peak was reached and the 2-year Treasury made a new high. Even longer-duration 10- BX:TMUBMUSD10Y and 30-year yields BX:TMUBMUSD30Y moved meaningfully higher.

data.title: Alterome Therapeutics Presents Preliminary Clinical Data from Ongoing Phase 1/1b Trial of ALTA3263 Demonstrating Antitumor Activity in KRAS-Mutant Colorectal and Pancreatic Cancers at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium
data.description:
Alterome Therapeutics Presents Preliminary Clinical Data from Ongoing Phase 1/1b Trial of ALTA3263 Demonstrating Antitumor Activity in KRAS-Mutant Colorectal and Pancreatic Cancers at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium

ALTA3263 plus cetuximab achieved a 31% objective response rate (ORR) and 94% disease control rate (DCR) in patients with advanced metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC), with responses observed across multiple KRAS mutations

ALTA3263 was generally well tolerated as monotherapy and in combination with cetuximab, supporting further evaluation in combination regimens

Alterome Therapeutics, Inc., a clinical-stage precision oncology company focused on discovering and developing alteration-specific therapeutics to address oncogenic drivers, today announced the presentation of the preliminary clinical data from the Phase 1 dose-escalation portion of its ongoing Phase 1/1b clinical trial evaluating ALTA3263, an orally available KRAS-selective, pan-mutant, active/inactive (ON/OFF) inhibitor, in adult patients with KRAS-mutant advanced solid tumors. These data are being presented today in a late-breaking oral session during the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics (ENA 2026) in Barcelona, Spain.

ALTA3263 was designed to inhibit a broad range of KRAS mutations while sparing wild-type HRAS and NRAS, a profile that may support its use in combination with anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitors, other standard-of-care treatments, and targeted therapies.

As of the September 18, 2026 data cutoff, ALTA3263 demonstrated antitumor activity both in combination with cetuximab in patients with advanced metastatic CRC and as monotherapy in patients with advanced metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Pharmacokinetic analyses demonstrated increased linear, approximately dose-proportional exposure from 100 mg to 400 mg twice daily, with exposure at 400 mg twice daily exceeding preclinical steady-state benchmarks. Clinical activity was observed across multiple KRAS mutations, including G12D, G12V, G12A, G13D and Q61H, with the majority of treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) reported as Grade 1 or Grade 2.

“Preliminary data from the Phase 1 dose-escalation portion of ALTA3263’s trial in CRC and PDAC patients demonstrate its potential to improve upon currently available therapies and address a broad range of KRAS mutations, potentially expanding treatment options for patients who remain in need of more effective and tolerable therapies,” said Leo Faoro, M.D., MBA, Chief Medical Officer of Alterome Therapeutics. “These results support our continued focus on advancing ALTA3263 in CRC and PDAC and provide a strong rationale to evaluate ALTA3263 in earlier lines of therapy in combination with standard-of-care regimens and targeted therapies.”

ALTA3263 shows potential to broaden targeted therapy in KRAS-mutant CRC

Approximately 50% of colorectal cancers harbor KRAS mutations, making CRC a KRAS-mutant tumor type with significant unmet need in the United States. The most prevalent mutations include KRAS G12D (33%), G12V (22%), G13D (14%), and G12C (7%). Currently approved KRAS-targeted treatment options are limited to patients with KRAS G12C mutations, underscoring the need for therapies that address a broader range of KRAS mutations.

Combining KRAS inhibition with anti-EGFR inhibition may enhance antitumor activity by blocking EGFR-mediated feedback signaling that can limit the effectiveness of KRAS inhibitors in colorectal cancer. The preliminary clinical activity observed with ALTA3263 plus cetuximab provides initial support for this combination strategy in KRAS-mutant CRC.

As of the September 18, 2026 data cutoff, 120 patients had received ALTA3263, including 80 patients treated with monotherapy and 40 patients treated in combination with cetuximab. Patients had received a median of two prior lines of systemic therapy in advanced setting (range: 0–9). Tumor types included PDAC (46%), CRC (42%), non-small cell lung cancer (10%), and others (3%). The distribution of KRAS mutations among enrolled patients was as follows: G12V (40%), G12D (38%), G12A (8%), G13D (7%), Q61H (4%) and other mutations (3%). The maximum tolerated dose has not been reached.

In the Phase 1 dose-escalation portion of the trial, ALTA3263 in combination with cetuximab demonstrated antitumor activity in patients with KRAS-mutant CRC. Among 16 response-evaluable patients treated with ALTA3263 at doses of 200 mg and 300 mg twice-daily in combination with cetuximab who initiated treatment at least 14 weeks before the September 18, 2026 data cutoff and who had a scan post-baseline:

  • Five patients achieved a partial response (four confirmed and one unconfirmed), resulting in an ORR of 31% (5/16);
  • 15 patients achieved disease control, resulting in a DCR of 94% (15/16);
  • Tumor regression was observed in 94% of patients with post-baseline target lesions assessment (15/16); and
  • Responses were observed across multiple KRAS mutations, supporting the design objective of achieving broad mutant allele coverage.

Among 40 patients treated with ALTA3263 plus cetuximab, the majority of TRAEs were mild to moderate (62%), and no patients discontinued treatment due to TRAEs. Grade 3 or higher TRAEs occurred in 33% of patients, and six patients (15%) required dose reductions of ALTA3263 due to TRAEs. The most common TRAEs were diarrhea (83%), dermatitis acneiform (68%), nausea (63%) and vomiting (45%). Grade 3 dermatitis acneiform occurred in 8% of patients. These preliminary findings support our continued evaluation of ALTA3263 in combination with cetuximab.

“The activity observed with ALTA3263 plus cetuximab in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer is particularly encouraging, with responses across multiple KRAS mutations in a setting where this level of activity has historically been difficult to achieve,” said David S. Hong, M.D., Deputy Chair of the Department of Investigational Cancer Therapeutics at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. “These early results suggest that ALTA3263, in combination with cetuximab, has the potential to provide a new treatment approach for patients with KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer, where targeted treatment options are limited.”

Early monotherapy activity and safety of ALTA3263 in PDAC support evaluation in earlier-line combination regimens

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is one of the deadliest cancers, with KRAS mutations present in more than 90% of PDAC cases. Despite recent advances in KRAS-directed therapy, there remains a need for targeted therapies with tolerability profiles that may support combination approaches in earlier lines of therapy. The preliminary monotherapy activity and tolerability observed with ALTA3263 support its continued evaluation in PDAC in combination with standard-of-care regimens and targeted therapies.

In the Phase 1 dose-escalation portion of the trial, ALTA3263 monotherapy demonstrated antitumor activity in patients with PDAC treated at doses of 400 mg or 600 mg twice daily. Among 13 response-evaluable patients who initiated treatment at least 14 weeks before the September 18, 2026 data cutoff and had a post-baseline scan:

  • Three patients achieved confirmed partial responses, resulting in a confirmed objective response rate (ORR) of 23% (3/13);
  • Disease control rate was 77% (10/13); and
  • Tumor regression was observed in 83% of patients with post-baseline target lesions assessment (10/12).

Across 80 patients treated with ALTA3263 monotherapy across all tumor types, Grade 3 or higher TRAEs were reported in 15% of patients. The most common TRAEs were diarrhea (51%), vomiting (46%), nausea (45%), and fatigue (31%), predominantly Grade 1 or 2. Dermatitis acneiform was reported in 11% of patients; all events were Grade 1 or 2. One dose-limiting toxicity of Grade 3 diarrhea was observed at 400mg twice daily during monotherapy dose escalation.

The Phase 1/1b, open-label, dose-escalation and multiple-cohort trial of ALTA3263 in adults with advanced solid tumor malignancies with KRAS mutations (NCT06835569) is continuing to enroll patients, with further evaluation of ALTA3263 planned in combination regimens and in earlier treatment settings.

About Alterome Therapeutics, Inc.

Alterome Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage precision oncology company focused on discovering and developing alteration-specific therapeutics to address oncogenic drivers. The Company’s lead therapeutic candidate, ALTA3263, is an orally available, KRAS-selective, pan-mutant inhibitor targeting a broad range of oncogenic KRAS mutations in both the active (ON) and inactive (OFF) states while sparing HRAS and NRAS proteins whose inhibition may contribute to treatment-related toxicities. ALTA3263 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1/1b trial in advanced solid tumors with an initial focus on KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Alterome is led by a team of precision oncology leaders with a history of discovering and developing novel oncology therapies. For more information, visit www.alterome.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

data.title: DTC2026 | World's First Mass Production of Ultrahigh-Mobility Oxide Technology Paves the Way for a New Generation of Displays

DTC2026 | World's First Mass Production of Ultrahigh-Mobility Oxide Technology Paves the Way for a New Generation of Displays

DTC2026 | World's First Mass Production of Ultrahigh-Mobility Oxide Technology Paves the Way for a New Generation of Displays

PR Newswire

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 20, 2026

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TCL CSOT became the world's first to achieve mass production of ultrahigh-mobility oxide technology (electron mobility of ~50 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) on an 8.6-generation line. The major technical breakthrough marks the first time high mobility oxide technology has gone beyond the 50 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ threshold in mass production, presenting exciting new possibilities in display applications.

| Keywords: Ultrahigh mobility, 50 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, 8.6-generation mass production, world's first ultrahigh-mobility oxide product

Beyond 50 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹: Premium Displays Without the Compromise

For years, the production of high-end displays has involved a series of trade-offs: high refresh rates versus lower power consumption, high resolution versus brightness, and narrow bezels versus cost. The mass production of ultrahigh-mobility oxide technology breaks this deadlock by enabling drive currents that surpass the critical threshold needed to deliver these properties without such compromises.

All-Round Excellence in Image Quality, Energy Efficiency, and Cost

Traditionally, gains in image quality have come at the expense of power consumption. However, the properties of ultrahigh-mobility oxide technology change this on several fronts. Firstly, like all oxide TFTs, the technology offers extremely low off-state current, enabling static images to be held at an ultra-low refresh rate, thereby reducing refresh power consumption. Secondly, higher current drive allows GOA (gate driver on array) and driver circuits to operate with lower voltage swings and shorter charging times. Combined with optimization across the full signal chain, power consumption is also reduced when displaying dynamic images. As a result, ultrahigh-mobility oxide technology allows for improvements in image quality without requiring extra power.

By enabling displays to switch between ultra-low and ultra-high refresh rates in the same panel, the technology also allows high-performance gaming and video applications to exist alongside power-efficient office and reading in one device.

Shrinking the TFT also increases aperture ratio, enabling higher pixel density without sacrificing brightness, so high-resolution screens no longer appear dim. Substantially reduced edge routing greatly improves the screen-to-body ratio, making ultra-narrow bezels a reality for mass-produced displays.

The real value of ultrahigh-mobility oxide technology is in turning what was once a series of trade-offs into a best-of-all-worlds scenario that delivers premium display experiences. Leveraging the scale of TCL CSOT's 8.6-generation production line, these premium displays can now be widely adopted at an affordable cost.

At DTC 2026, TCL CSOT unveiled its own ultrahigh-mobility display technology, setting a new standard for display excellence that will redefine the future for both consumer and professional display applications.

Technology Reimagined: A Seamless Loop from Process to Product

Developing ultrahigh-mobility oxide technology is the result of significant engineering achievements made by TCL CSOT and the team at the Institute of Science Tokyo's MDX Research Center for Element Strategy, led by Prof. Hideo Hosono. Together with Prof. Hosono's team, TCL CSOT has advanced the technology across three fronts—film deposition, device design, and architecture—transforming isolated processes into manufacturable products.

Film Deposition: Ultra-Uniform Oxide Semiconductor System

TCL CSOT has taken film deposition beyond conventional processes with the use of continuous rotary-target sputtering and a composite stacked oxide layer design that suppresses defects. A defect repair process further improves the interface, overcoming the stability challenges associated with ultrahigh-mobility materials.

| Key Metrics: Film thickness uniformity U% < 5%, average mobility 51.6 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹

Device Core: Precise Control of the Hydrogen–Oxygen Balance in the Insulator

Ultrahigh-mobility devices are highly sensitive to moisture, hydrogen, and oxygen, and any deviation from the optimal hydrogen–oxygen ratio in the insulator can degrade performance. To address this, TCL CSOT has developed a hydrogen–oxygen balance control system for both the front- and back-channel insulators, providing threefold protection.

New Circuit Architecture Unlocks the Potential of Ultrahigh-Mobility Oxide

Alongside its clear benefits, higher mobility also brings new challenges, including weaker gate control, threshold-voltage drift, and increased self-heating. To address these challenges, TCL CSOT has introduced a new GOA architecture alongside optimized device design and improved thermal management to enable the full potential of ultrahigh-mobility oxide to be realized.

Redefining the Limits of LCD Technology

The mass production of ultrahigh-mobility oxide technology gives LCD a major competitive edge in applications such as high-refresh-rate notebooks and high-end monitors, enabling it to compete directly with OLED. Its inherent advantages—low cost, long lifetimes, and no burn-in—combined with high image quality and low power consumption, will offer users a wider choice of high-quality options at a lower price point compared with OLED.

Meanwhile, ultrahigh-mobility oxide technology also shows strong potential in emerging areas such as VR/AR, medical displays, and automotive displays, where its high refresh rates can help reduce motion sickness, its high color fidelity meets high professional requirements, and its high reliability supports use in diverse environments.

From the Laboratory to the Production Line

TCL CSOT has built extensive expertise in oxide technology over the years, progressing from mass production of conventional IGZO in 2024 to 30 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ high-mobility oxide in 2025, and achieving mass production of ultrahigh-mobility oxide in 2026. The latest breakthrough combines device stability comparable to conventional IGZO with excellent voltage endurance and reliability, marking a major step from the laboratory to production and lays the foundations for future product iterations and scale expansion.

About TCL CSOT

Established in 2009, TCL China Star Optoelectronics Technology Co., Ltd. (TCL CSOT) is a leading global innovator in display technologies. Its LCD, OLED, and MLED solutions power applications across TVs, smartphones, tablets, laptops, monitors, automotive systems, VR/XR, and commercial displays. With a clear strategic direction set by its advanced display technology brand APEX, TCL CSOT invests continuously and strategically in R&D, driven by a mission to amaze, protect and inspire all people through endlessly innovative display technology. As part of TCL's Worldwide Olympic Partnership, TCL CSOT is proud to deliver display solutions that elevate experiences on the global stage.

data.title: Gold, Silver Drop to Lowest Levels in Over a Year — Update
data.description:
By Megan Cheah and Farhan Rafid

Gold and silver fell to their lowest levels in over a year on Friday as expectations of higher interest rates globally and a broader selloff across commodities pressured precious metals.

Expectations for tighter monetary policy appear to have overshadowed the typical demand for gold as a safe haven for risk-averse investors. The precious metals weakened despite heavy losses across Asian stock markets.

December gold futures fell 3% to $3,573.60 a troy ounce, while spot silver declined around 0.8% to $42.42 an ounce.

The decline in precious metals is part of a broader selloff across commodities, with investors cutting exposure, unwinding crowded positions and taking profits ahead of year-end, according to Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank.

Hansen said in a note Friday that precious metals had suffered the largest losses, with silver falling 14% and gold nearly 8% this week. Rising borrowing costs, a stronger U.S. dollar and concerns about artificial-intelligence investment have added to selling pressure, while losses in other assets have increased demand for cash.

Gold's failure to attract safe-haven demand during the equity-market selloff suggests investors are selling liquid assets to cover losses and reduce risk, Hansen said. However, holdings in gold exchange-traded funds have remained broadly unchanged over the past month despite the decline in prices, indicating longer-term investors have largely maintained their exposure.

The gold-to-silver ratio climbed to 85.58 Friday, about 25% above its average over nearly three decades. The ratio measures how many ounces of silver are needed to buy an ounce of gold, with a higher reading indicating silver is relatively cheaper.

Carsten Menke, head of Next Generation Research at Julius Baer, said silver's decline below $45 an ounce, alongside a gold-to-silver ratio above 85, could present a buying opportunity. However, the bank is waiting for signs that prices have bottomed before turning more positive, as further declines remain possible. Julius Baer maintains a neutral view on silver and a constructive outlook for gold.

Copper also declined, with December futures falling 1.6% to $5.5460 a pound. The industrial metal is on track to lose around 9% this week, reaching an eight-month low amid concerns about global growth, Chinese demand and the outlook for artificial-intelligence infrastructure investment, according to Saxo Bank.

Julius Baer upgraded its outlook for copper to constructive following the recent correction, saying the metal remains at risk of a structural supply deficit as demand from electric vehicles, clean energy and battery storage increases. Copper prices have fallen more than 15% from their highs this year, but the bank expects electrification-related technologies to account for around 30% of demand by 2035, compared with 25% in 2025. Menke said mining investments are increasing but might come too late to prevent a shortage.

Japan's consumer inflation data for October released Friday showed prices were accelerating past the Bank of Japan's target. That reinforced expectations for tighter policy as policymakers grew increasingly worried about the risk of higher prices due to increased energy costs, persistent yen weakness and rising semiconductor prices amid the artificial-intelligence boom.

"A rate hike at the next meeting in December looks highly likely, and the central bank will likely discuss an additional increase in March 2027, when inflation is expected to accelerate into the 3% range," said Takeshi Minami, an economist at Norinchukin Research Institute.

Minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve's October meeting released Wednesday also showed that nearly all policymakers expected higher interest rates would be needed to lower inflation.

The minutes "showed strong alignment from Fed officials on the need for additional rate hikes," said MUFG analysts. Markets recently priced in a 93% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month.

Many also expect the European Central Bank to raise rates in December after staying on hold last month, as it is under pressure to address the inflationary backdrop given persistently high energy prices.

A higher interest-rate environment typically diminishes the allure of nonyielding assets such as gold and silver. The hawkish Fed view also likely lifted the dollar, which makes gold and silver, both dollar-denominated commodities, more expensive for investors holding other currencies.

Upcoming U.S. economic data could shape expectations for the size of a December interest-rate move by the Fed, said Critical Metals' Tony Sage in a note. This includes the second estimate for the country's third-quarter gross domestic product growth due next week.

"Firm readings could lift yields further and extend gold's losses, while softer prints may offer some relief," he added.
